description.value: The study examined brain responses to photographs of foods differing in calorie content in healthy normal-weight women, focusing on common and calorie-specific cortical and limbic activation.

spans.text: Therefore, we applied functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to study the cerebral responses of 13 healthy normal-weight adult women as they viewed color photographs of food.
No fMRI study of healthy normal-weight individuals has examined the question of how the brain responds to visual presentations of foods that differ in their energy value (i.e., calorie content).

design.value: Three visual activation tasks were presented over separate scanning runs: low-calorie foods, high-calorie foods, and nonedible food-related utensils; each paradigm consisted of alternating stimulation and control blocks, and task order was counterbalanced across subjects.

spans.text: Three visual activation tasks were presented over separate scanning runs: (1) low-calorie foods, (2) high-calorie foods, and (3) nonedible food-related utensils.
The order of presentation of the three tasks was counterbalanced across subjects.
Each of these paradigms lasted for 150 sec, consisting of two 30-sec stimulation periods, which alternated with three control blocks of equal duration.
